answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a scarce, time-locked stake, with rewards released only after its claims survive challenges from randomly selected peers. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the attacker’s stake or influence; each account must lock more capital and risk losing it when evidence exposes fabricated work. A lantern may reveal an echo of copied claims, while willow-like branching identities still face the same costly bond and delayed payout.
